title: Signal Accordion — Sales/CS Batch Intake and Rapid Implementation Sketch
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Sales and Customer Success are submitting high-volume, heterogeneous enterprise feature requests (non-bug) that arrive as single-item asks, multi-account bundles, and follow-ups. PMs spend 30–90 minutes per request just to normalize fields, group related asks, and produce a first-pass feasibility note. This creates backlog, noisy prioritization signals, and missed canary opportunities for Dedicated/Private customers.

Goal: Build a lightweight 'Signal Accordion' workflow that folds similar Sales/CS requests into coherent bundles, applies a deterministic first-pass scoping rubric, and emits a short implementation sketch + econ proxy for PM and Eng review within one business day. The output must be legible to PMs, intake reps, and Solutions Engineers.

Scope: non-bug product feature asks originating from Sales/CS. Includes: normalization rules, automatic similarity grouping (rule-based + simple vector match), quick econ heuristics, and a templated 'first-pass sketch' artifact stored in Confluence/Drive and referenced from the Linear ticket. Excludes: security-sensitive asks requiring legal review, full architecture designs, and formal SLA negotiations (these escalate to Enterprise Pathway).

Why now: volume of enterprise feature asks has increased 2.4x YTD; current manual process is a bottleneck for Product's ability to surface repeatable product signals and to triage Dedicated/Private readiness. This is a low-risk, high-leverage intervention to reduce noise and accelerate PM decision cycles.
acceptance_criteria: Signal Accordion pipeline ingests Sales/CS submission form and normalizes required fields (account, product area, ask type, urgency) with >95% accuracy based on validation tests.
Automatic grouping reduces number of duplicate/semi-duplicate tickets by at least 40% in a 2-week A/B window versus control.
First-pass sketch template (problem, user, rough solution, estimated effort bucket, business impact) is auto-populated and attached to the Linear ticket within 24 hours for 90% of incoming asks.
Solutions Engineering and Sales report improved handoffs: median follow-up clarifying questions per ticket drops by >=30%.
Bundle-level econ proxy (T-shirt effort, potential ARR uplift band) appears for grouped asks and is understandable by Sales without additional PM intervention.
decisions: Use a hybrid rule-based + lightweight vector similarity (open-source embeddings in initial phase) to avoid heavy infra lift for ML ops.
Implement grouping at a daily batch cadence rather than strictly real-time to keep alerts manageable and to allow human review queues.
Keep the initial econ proxy intentionally coarse (bands: Negligible / Small / Medium / Large) to avoid false precision and to accelerate decisions.
Store generated sketches in a shared Drive folder and add link to Linear ticket rather than creating a new system of record.
Rollout first to North America accounts for one month before region expansion to EU/APAC to monitor privacy/regulatory edge-cases.
tradeoffs: Rule-based + vector approach reduces false positives early but may miss nuanced semantic duplicates; acceptable as short-term compromise.
Daily batching reduces signal immediacy but limits churn and reviewer fatigue; tradeoff favors review quality over instant grouping.
Coarse econ bands speed deployment but sacrifice per-account financial precision; will iterate with Sales for high-value accounts.
